beliefs: f adds 1 to the ASCII code of every character, not just letters (a→b, z→{, A→B, Z→[, space→!, digit→next digit) [E1, E2]
Because it's a raw +1 on all characters, 'z' becomes '{' and 'Z' becomes '[' rather than wrapping to 'a'/'A' [E2]
Case is preserved trivially since each char shifts independently [E1, E2]
notes: The outputs show every character (letters, digits, spaces, punctuation) incremented by one in ASCII: 'z'→'{', 'Z'→'[', ' '→'!', '9'→':', '!'→'"'. So it's a blanket +1 on ord(ch), not an alphabet shift with wraparound.
